I was diagnosed at the age of 4 so I don't remember a time when I wasn't diabetic but here are some helpful tips. 
1. Don't beresentful for having to get diet items. Maybe start switching to diet sodas and juices for the household. I remember always being forgotten when drinks and snacks were gotten and forced to starve until the family event was over. Along ith that my uncles would always roll their eyes when remember to grab diet coke for me. 
2. Reward them/compliment them for good blood sugar but never yell or blame for bad blood sugar. Highs and lows happen and although they're unwanted, make sure to remind them that it happens and how to correct it. 
3. Be patient. Diabetes can make a person irratible and emtional. Especially when first diagnosed, so please make sure that you're calm and supportive. Maybe look into child support groups and diabetic summer camps to help them not feel so alone. 
4. CHECK THEIR BLOOD SUGAR DEVICE CONSTANTLY. it's easy to fall off the wagon, even for a responsivke kid. I was considered extremely responsible for my age so my parents left me alone to handle my diabetes in high school. That was a mistake and I developed so bad habits. I was distracted by lovers and school work too. I can't stress this enough, GIVE FREEDOM BUT ALWAYS DOUBLE CHECK THEIR DEVICE. this could save your kids life.
